title: review: F7: bus.db() leaks one sqlite connection per call; ResourceWarnings from the leaks break test_handover's stderr count in the gate
spec:
Finding 2026-09-19 19:40 (T-0254 gate red three times on tests/test_handover.py::test_handover_survives_jev_exception with AssertionError 272..365 != 2): orchestrator/bus.py:42 db() opens a new sqlite3.Connection on every call and _save()/_event() (lines 50-59) call db().execute(...) without ever closing it, so every bus write leaks a connection until garbage collection. Under `python -W always::ResourceWarning -m unittest tests.test_cli tests.test_handover` about 130 'ResourceWarning: unclosed database in <sqlite3.Connection>' lines appear; when the collector runs inside handover.write() while the test has redirect_stderr active, the test's assertion that stderr has exactly rank.call_count lines fails. It reproduces with tests.test_cli or tests.test_planner_runs before tests.test_handover (both gained tests that create many bus tasks in Phase F) and is invisible when test_handover runs alone.
Change:
1. orchestrator/bus.py: make the connection lifetime explicit. Either a module-level cached connection per STATE path (re-opened when STATE changes, which tests do) that is closed at interpreter exit via atexit, or db() as a contextlib.contextmanager that closes on exit, with _save/_event/and every other db() caller using `with db() as c:`. Pick the smaller diff that leaves zero unclosed connections; keep create-table-if-not-exists semantics and isolation_level=None. Search the package for every db() caller (grep "db()" orchestrator/ tests/ .claude/) and adapt them.
2. tests/test_bus.py (create if absent): test_db_leaves_no_unclosed_connection: run a few create_task/update/post_result calls under warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) with simplefilter('always', ResourceWarning) followed by gc.collect(), assert no ResourceWarning mentioning sqlite3.Connection was recorded.
3. tests/test_handover.py::test_handover_survives_jev_exception (about line 314): count only the lines that start with 'handover:' instead of every stderr line, so an unrelated warning from garbage collection cannot fail this test again; keep the rank.call_count == 2 assertion.
Report in the final message the number of db() call sites changed and the ResourceWarning count before and after under -W always::ResourceWarning for tests.test_cli tests.test_handover.
acceptance: uv run --project . python -W always::ResourceWarning -m unittest tests.test_cli tests.test_handover prints zero lines containing 'unclosed database' and the suite passes
uv run --project . python -m unittest tests.test_planner_runs tests.test_handover passes (the pair that failed before)
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: atexit.register(_close_db) closes the shared connection without acquiring _connection_lock. If a daemon worker thread is still mid-execute() against the bus during interpreter shutdown, this can race and raise sqlite3.ProgrammingError('Cannot operate on a closed database'). Narrow window, not covered by the given acceptance tests, but worth a lock/guard given the code's own comment that worker threads share this connection.
